extracted.intended_audience: Investigators applying for or reviewing NIH R01 grant applications (NIH/NIAID peer review participants)
extracted.subtask_description: This is an NIH/NIAID R01 summary statement describing the review criteria and reviewers' written critiques used to evaluate an R01 application (Significance, Investigators, Innovation, Approach, Environment, plus administrative/ethical checks and scoring rules). It is aimed at guiding applicants and reviewers on what is judged and why.

rubrics_metrics.name: Overall Impact (Overall Impact score)
rubrics_metrics.description: Overall Impact: reviewers provide an overall impact assessment describing the likelihood that the project will exert a sustained, powerful influence on the research field(s) involved. The summary statement gives an overall qualitative statement and an overall impact score.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples in critiques show reviewers synthesize strengths and weaknesses across criteria (e.g., novelty, focus, preliminary data, coordination concerns) to justify the overall enthusiasm or reservations. Scoring note: the impact/priority score is calculated after discussion by averaging the overall scores (1-9) given by all voting reviewers on the committee and multiplying by 10.

rubrics_metrics.name: Significance
rubrics_metrics.description: Significance: Does the project address an important problem or critical barrier in the field? Will successful completion of the aims change scientific knowledge, technical capability, clinical practice, or have translational/public health impact?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewer examples: strengths include novelty of investigating biofilm structural/physical properties and potential to enable new control strategies and therapeutics. Weakness examples include missing or unclear elements (none explicitly in some critiques). The Public Health Relevance section also ties significance to NIH mission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Investigator(s)
rubrics_metrics.description: Investigator(s): Are the PD/PI, collaborators, and other researchers well suited, trained, and capable of carrying out the proposed work? Is the team appropriately organized and interactive?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewer comments include praise for an outstanding, collaborative, interdisciplinary team and for publication records; weaknesses include lack of clearly defined specific tasks for each investigator and questions about coordination among groups. The application is labeled as NEW INVESTIGATOR where relevant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Innovation
rubrics_metrics.description: Innovation: Does the application challenge and seek to shift current research or clinical practice paradigms through novel theoretical concepts, approaches or methodologies, instrumentation, or interventions?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers cite development of novel techniques to study biofilms, focus on structural/mechanical properties, new imaging and manipulative techniques, and fresh approaches to neutrophil–biofilm interactions as innovative strengths. Few weaknesses were noted for innovation in this application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Approach
rubrics_metrics.description: Approach: Are the overall strategy, methodology, and analyses well-reasoned and appropriate to accomplish the specific aims? Are potential problems and alternative strategies addressed?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Detailed strengths noted: use of in vivo models, selection of mutants, multiple disease outcome assays, quantitative imaging (CLSM), AFM, microrheology, quantum dots, biomimetic biofilms, sequential aims. Weaknesses/concerns include coordination among labs, unclear imaging plans for Aim 1, reliance on in vitro tests where in vivo might be preferable, animal use inconsistencies (mouse needed but not described in approach), AFM-specific issues (adhesion between tip and biofilms), and how films will be removed without disrupting structure. End-point measurements were noted as clearly defined.

rubrics_metrics.name: Environment
rubrics_metrics.description: Environment: Will the scientific environment in which the work will be done contribute to the probability of success? Are institutional support, equipment, and other resources available?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers repeatedly noted excellent environments at UT Austin and partner institutions, availability of necessary equipment and facilities, and synergistic partnering. No major weaknesses were generally noted for environment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Protections for Human Subjects
rubrics_metrics.description: Protections for Human Subjects: Assessment of human subjects protections and applicability (including whether human subjects are involved).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For this application reviewers marked 'Not Applicable (No Human Subjects)'. When applicable, reviewers evaluate protections and compliance with human subjects policies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Vertebrate Animals
rubrics_metrics.description: Vertebrate Animals: Evaluation of the vertebrate animal section for welfare concerns, justification of animal use, and adherence to required points (all four points addressed).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewer notes show variable determinations: one reviewer noted 'NO, animal welfare concerns or incomplete' because a mouse is required for Aim 3 but not described in approach; other reviewers indicated 'YES, all four points addressed' and the Scientific Review Officer summarized 'VERTEBRATE ANIMAL: ACCEPTABLE'. Guidance includes ensuring least number of animals used and that animal procedures are described in the approach.

rubrics_metrics.name: Biohazards
rubrics_metrics.description: Biohazards: Assessment of whether biological agents or materials will be handled safely and appropriately (biosafety measures).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers indicated 'Acceptable' for biohazards with specific comment that Pseudomonas will be handled in appropriate biosafety hoods. When applicable, reviewers check for adequate biosafety practices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Resubmission (Amended Application) Response
rubrics_metrics.description: Resubmission: For amended applications, reviewers assess whether the application adequately responds to prior reviewers' comments and whether revisions are clearly denoted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewer comments: 'It is a much-improved submission...'; 'The application has responded well to SS critique.' Also a weakness noted that alterations from the original should be but were not clearly denoted within the Research Plan. NIH policy note referenced about resubmissions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Resource Sharing Plans
rubrics_metrics.description: Resource Sharing Plans: Evaluation of plans for sharing data, resources, meetings, and data exchange necessary for the project and the broader research community.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewer assessments varied from 'Unacceptable' (e.g., 'proposed meetings and data exchange is not sufficient for such complex projects') to 'Acceptable'. Reviewers expect sufficient plans for meetings and data exchange when projects are complex and collaborative.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authentication of Key Biological and/or Chemical Resources
rubrics_metrics.description: Authentication of Key Biological and/or Chemical Resources: Assessment of plans to ensure identity and validity of critical biological reagents and chemical resources.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewer entries include 'Not Applicable' for some sections and 'Acceptable' for others. When applicable, reviewers check for authentication procedures and their adequacy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Budget and Period of Support / Administrative Budget Note
rubrics_metrics.description: Budget and Period of Support: Review of the recommended budget, recommended modifications, and whether budget justification is complete. Administrative Budget Note clarifies that budgets shown are requested and may be adjusted by institute grants management staff.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewer comments included 'Recommended budget modifications or possible overlap identified' and 'Certain portions of budget justification are missing. Support for several graduate students/postdocs is requested without clearly defined tasks.' Elsewhere reviewers recommended 'Recommend as Requested' and the committee recommended the budget 'as requested.' Administrative note: 'The budget shown is the requested budget and has not been adjusted to reflect any recommendations made by reviewers. If an award is planned, the costs will be calculated by Institute grants management staff based on the recommendations outlined below in the COMMITTEE BUDGET RECOMMENDATIONS section.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Scoring procedures and calculation (criteria vs overall score)
rubrics_metrics.description: Scoring procedures: Criterion scores (Significance, Investigator(s), Innovation, Approach, Environment) are submitted by individual reviewers prior to the meeting and are not discussed specifically at the meeting; the overall/impact score is calculated after discussion by averaging overall scores and multiplying by 10.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: From footnote: 'The impact/priority score is calculated after discussion of an application by averaging the overall scores (1-9) given by all voting reviewers on the committee and multiplying by 10. The criterion scores are submitted prior to the meeting by the individual reviewers assigned to an application, and are not discussed specifically at the review meeting or calculated into the overall impact score.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Public Health Relevance
rubrics_metrics.description: Public Health Relevance: A statement on how the proposed research is relevant to public health and to NIH's mission to foster fundamental creative discoveries and innovative research strategies as a basis for protecting health.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewer/applicant language ties project significance to potential development of new diagnostics and treatments for chronic biofilm infections and relevance to NIH's mission to protect health through innovation and discoveries.
